samples.question: The picture is a measurement sheet on white paper. Exactly three marks are drawn in pure black: two short black vertical ticks of equal height, and one black horizontal measuring bar that lies in a separate row so that white paper always separates it from the ticks. Everything else - the pale grey ruler along the top, the coloured vertical ticks, the coloured bars and the coloured squares - is decoration and carries no information; only the three black marks matter. The span is the horizontal distance between the centres of the two black ticks. The measuring bar's length is its own horizontal width. Copies of the measuring bar are laid end to end starting at one black tick and running towards the other, never overlapping and never reaching past the far tick. How many whole copies of the black measuring bar fit inside the span? Answer with a single whole number: 2, 3, or 4.
